description: Six-panel composite of ThermoCalc (TCFE9) equilibrium phase-fraction (CALPHAD) calculations for the Fe-8Mn-0.2C system with systematic Al and Si additions. Every panel plots Volume Fraction (y-axis, 0-1.0) against Temperature (°C) (x-axis, 0-1400) with an identical legend: BCC (black), CEMENTITE (red), FCC (blue), LIQUID (magenta), M23C6 (green). Each panel also carries a shaded yellow band marking the intercritical (ICT) region bounded below by 600 °C and with an upper bound printed on the panel. (a) "0-Al", band 600-688 °C; (b) "1-Al", 600-730 °C; (c) "2-Al", 600-789 °C; (d) "3-Al", 600-900 °C; (e) "4-Al", 600-980 °C, where the FCC curve peaks near 0.7 around 950 °C while BCC passes through a minimum of about 0.25 and a δ label appears near 1050 °C; (f) "3-Al 1-Si", 600-1000 °C, also annotated δ, with FCC peaking near 0.6. In (a)-(d), BCC falls and FCC rises steeply across the band; at high Al (e, f) BCC re-rises at high temperature as the δ-ferrite field. The figure demonstrates that Al widens the ICT window and that 4Al or 3Al+1Si introduces δ-ferrite into the ICT range, which drives the choice of Fe-8Mn-3Al-0.2C and Fe-8Mn-3Al-1Si-0.2C for study.

subfigures.description: Equilibrium phase fractions for '0-Al' (Fe-8Mn-0.2C). BCC (black) starts near 0.92 at low temperature and falls steeply; FCC (blue) rises from ~0.05 near 500 °C to 1.0 by ~700 °C. Small CEMENTITE (red, ~0.03) and M23C6 (green) fractions persist at low temperature. Yellow shaded ICT band labelled 600-688 °C.
Same axes and legend for '1-Al'. BCC-to-FCC crossover shifts slightly to higher temperature; FCC reaches 1.0 near 730 °C. Yellow ICT band labelled 600-730 °C.
'2-Al': the BCC decline begins earlier and reaches ~0 near 800 °C, FCC reaching 1.0 at ~800 °C; above ~1350 °C FCC drops again and BCC rises. Yellow ICT band labelled 600-789 °C.
'3-Al': FCC reaches 1.0 at about 900 °C; above ~1150 °C the BCC curve rises again to ~0.85 at 1400 °C. Yellow ICT band labelled 600-900 °C.

'4-Al': FCC rises to a maximum of about 0.7 near 950 °C, then falls; BCC drops to a minimum near 0.25 and rises again at high temperature, with a δ annotation on the re-rising BCC branch. LIQUID (magenta) appears near 1400 °C. Yellow ICT band labelled 600-980 °C.

'3-Al 1-Si': FCC peaks at about 0.6 near 950 °C and BCC shows a shallow minimum (~0.35) with a δ annotation; BCC rises to ~1.0 at 1400 °C. Yellow ICT band labelled 600-1000 °C. Top edge of the panel is slightly cropped.

observations.observation: All six panels share identical axes: Volume Fraction (0 to 1.0) versus Temperature (°C) from 0 to 1400.
The legend common to all panels lists five phases: BCC (black), CEMENTITE (red), FCC (blue), LIQUID (magenta) and M23C6 (green).

Each panel contains a shaded yellow band marking the intercritical temperature range, with the numerical bounds printed above the band as 600-688 °C (a), 600-730 °C (b), 600-789 °C (c), 600-900 °C (d), 600-980 °C (e) and 600-1000 °C (f).
Panel (a) is labelled '0-Al' and panel (e) '4-Al'; the FCC fraction in (e) peaks at roughly 0.7 near 950 °C while BCC passes a minimum of about 0.25 before rising again.
A δ annotation appears on the high-temperature re-rising BCC branch in panels (e) '4-Al' and (f) '3-Al 1-Si'.
In every panel, CEMENTITE and M23C6 fractions remain small (below about 0.05 volume fraction) and are largely confined to the low-temperature region; LIQUID appears only close to 1400 °C.
The caption states that the lower critical temperature is taken as 600 °C for all compositions, considering the limited diffusion capacity of Mn at lower temperatures.
The caption states that the intercritical temperature range increases from 88 °C for 0Al to 300 °C for 3Al.
The caption states that when Al is increased to 4 %, δ-ferrite is also introduced as an equilibrium phase in the ICT range, and that adding 1 % Si to the 3Al system has a similar effect.
The citing text states that these thermodynamic calculations were performed with ThermoCalc using the TCFE9 steel database.

The citing text states that two compositions were selected from these predictions for microstructural and mechanical study: Fe-8Mn-3Al-0.2C (maximum Al without δ-ferrite) and Fe-8Mn-3Al-1Si-0.2C (Si addition with δ-ferrite).

The citing text states that the significantly higher amount of ferrite, especially δ-ferrite, observed in the M2 steel is expected according to the thermodynamic predictions in Fig. 1d, f owing to the presence of Si.
